name: Innuitian Region

geo.extent: Queen Elizabeth Islands (Ellesmere, Axel Heiberg and neighbouring islands)

description: The mountains, plateaus and lowlands of the northern Arctic islands: two mountain zones (Grantland, Axel Heiberg, Victoria and Albert mountains) separated by the Eureka Upland, with ice sheets on Axel Heiberg and north-western Ellesmere islands through which peaks rise as nunataks; Sverdrup Lowlands and Perry Plateau to the south. Barbeau Peak (2,616 m) on Ellesmere Island is Nunavut's highest point.

notable_heights.name: Barbeau Peak, Ellesmere Island (highest point of Nunavut)

attributes.ecozone_named_in_source: Arctic Cordillera (mountains; mainly unvegetated; extremely cold, dry; continuous permafrost)

sources.title: The Atlas of Canada – Physiographic Regions of Canada (map 1254A compiled by H.S. Bostock, 1967, with descriptive text)

limitations: Physiographic description summarised from the Atlas of Canada; the map dates from 1967 (Bostock) and boundaries are generalised at 1:5 million. Lat/lon not given because the record describes an extensive region, not a point. The Arctic Cordillera ecozone also includes the mountains of eastern Baffin Island and the Torngats (Davis Region of the Shield in the physiographic scheme).
